subject: ChatGPT lands on Linux with Codex while Claude's hidden thinking expos
intro: AI is moving to your desktop, fast. OpenAI just landed on Linux, Unsloth ships local training for everyone, and the whole industry is racing to own your machine. The irony? Just as agents get closer to your files and repos, researchers found that the "encrypted" reasoning those same agents produce is basically a shared secret anyone can decode. Closer access, bigger blast radius. We're watching a platform war play out in real time, and security is already playing catch-up.

summary.headline: Security flaw lets anyone steal hidden reasoning from Claude, GPT, and Gemini
OpenAI drops ChatGPT desktop app for Linux on Ubuntu, Debian, and Fedora
Unsloth releases open-source desktop app to run and train models 2x faster locally

news.headline: Security flaw lets anyone steal hidden reasoning from Claude, GPT, and Gemini
news.body: AI companies hide their models' step-by-step thinking inside encrypted blobs sent back to your client. Sounds safe. It isn't. Researchers found that these encrypted chunks are fully portable. Grab a blob from Claude Opus, inject it into the cheaper, less guarded Haiku, and Haiku will just... read it out loud. No breaking encryption needed. The same trick works on OpenAI and Gemini. Here's what this actually unlocks for attackers: If you ever shared a Claude Code or Codex session publicly, those encrypted blobs are decodable. The labs have patched several issues after responsible disclosure.
bullets: Steal proprietary reasoning traces from top models using weaker ones as a decoder
Extract private data from public session logs. A scan of ~7,000 public traces found 62 API keys , 33 emails, and 33 passwords
Surface hidden hazardous info the model rejected in its visible reply but reasoned through internally
Inject invisible malicious instructions inside encrypted blobs to poison shared agent workflows

news.headline: OpenAI drops ChatGPT desktop app for Linux on Ubuntu, Debian, and Fedora
news.body: For years, ChatGPT had a desktop app on Mac and Windows. Linux? Nothing. That gap just closed. OpenAI dropped a preview of the official ChatGPT desktop app for Linux. This is not a browser wrapper or a CLI tool. It is a full native app, and it ships with three things bundled together: That last one is the big deal. Codex running natively on Linux means the agent lives right where your code does. Supported distros: Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, Fedora 43 and 44. Install via .deb or .rpm packages for x64 or ARM64. The installer also adds an OpenAI repo so updates flow through apt automatically. It is free to download, but some features need a paid plan.
bullets: ChatGPT - the assistant you already know
ChatGPT Work - for team and workplace tasks
Codex - an AI coding agent that can read your local files, run inside your actual repos, and control apps on your machine

news.headline: Unsloth releases open-source desktop app to run and train models 2x faster locally
news.body: Running AI models on your own machine just got a proper app. Unsloth Desktop is an open-source desktop app that lets you run and train AI models locally, on Mac, Windows, and Linux, no cloud required. Your data never leaves your machine. That's the whole point. Here's what you actually get: The big unlock here: you can build AI-powered apps, run experiments, and fine-tune models without paying per API call or sending sensitive data anywhere. It's on GitHub and their website right now, free to grab.
bullets: Train models 2x faster using 70% less GPU memory, so even mid-range hardware works
Connect Claude Code or Codex to local models instead of paid APIs
Private web search, deep research, and RAG (feeding your own documents to the model)
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Apple Silicon GPUs
Export models in standard formats like GGUF for easy sharing
